title: Field-fibre points and geometric stabilizer-isomorphism locus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the categories over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, their fibre categories and morphisms of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and the quotient point set $|F|$ of field-valued objects of [def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties]. Let $F,G$ be such categories over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. The point class of an object $x$ in the fibre over an $S$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$, where $K$ is a field, is its quotient class $\operatorname{pt}(x)\in|F|$. For a morphism $f:F\to G$ of categories over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, define its geometric stabilizer-isomorphism locus to be the subset of $|F|$ consisting of classes $p$ for which there exist an algebraically closed field $\Omega$, an $S$-structure on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and an object $x$ in that fibre of $F$ such that $\operatorname{pt}(x)=p$ and the map $\operatorname{Aut}(x)\to\operatorname{Aut}(f(x))$ induced by the actual fibre functor is bijective. For Deligne--Mumford stacks this is the locus where $f$ induces an isomorphism on geometric stabilizer group algebraic spaces, since these stabilizers over an algebraically closed field are etale. This definition asserts no openness or global stabilizer preservation.
